description: What Heeler types into a tmux Pane (ADR 0043), and what the Pane's program read for it, per tmux version, `extended-keys` setting, `extended-keys-format` (from 3.5) and the keyboard mode the program asked for. `keys` holds 65 keys as keytest.py named them: `desktop` is xterm's encoding of the key, which a pty attached as an ordinary tmux client wrote, standing in for a desktop terminal, and which TmuxKeyReader reads back; `key` is the tmux name Heeler sends for it, `extended` whether it has no legacy encoding (sent only while `#{pane_key_mode}` reads `Ext 1` or `Ext 2`), and `text` the text Heeler sends with `send-keys -l` in place of a key. Each run's `read` is what a probe program in the Pane read, in hex, when the desktop typed each key (empty: nothing); `heelerRead` is what it read for Heeler's `send-keys` where that differs from `read`; `paneKeyMode` is `#{pane_key_mode}` with the program running (3.3a has no such format and reads empty). `program` is the mode the probe asked for: none (`legacy`), modifyOtherKeys 1 or 2 (`mok1`, `mok2`), or kitty's flags 5 (`kitty`). `texts` are arguments in tmux's double-quoted form, and `literal` whether each arrived exactly through `send-keys -l` from a control client (`received` in hex when not); `pastes` the same for `set-buffer` and `paste-buffer -d` with `flags`, with the probe's bracketed paste on or off. `oneShot` is a `send-keys -l --` argument given as an argv word of a one-shot `tmux` command and the text that arrived. Sources: `keys-3.3a` and `keys-3.7b` are keytest.py's runs of 2026-11-10 on macOS 27.0 (ADR 0043's Evidence) against tmux 3.3a built from its release tarball and Homebrew's tmux 3.7b, the probe's keyboard mode set before a desktop client attached, escape-time 10; `modes-3.3a` and `modes-3.7b` are a re-measurement of 2026-11-11 on the same Mac and builds, in the same way, of what keymode.py had found but not kept: `#{pane_key_mode}`, the reads for `C-BTab`, `C-S-A` and `C-S-V` (Heeler's names for keytest.py's `C-S-Tab`, `C-S-a` and `C-S-v`, whose desktop reads it matched), and the one-shot arguments; `text-3.3a` and `text-3.7b` are texttest.py's runs of 2026-11-10 through a control client, the probe asking for modifyOtherKeys 2 and bracketed paste.
